stem: A young infant looks unwell and has an apparent upper respiratory tract infection on examination; what is the best next step in sepsis assessment?

options.text: Accept the URTI as the source and avoid further sepsis assessment
Assess for possible serious bacterial infection despite the apparent URTI
Limit management to antipyretics and fluids
Delay assessment unless the infant becomes febrile
Only investigate if there is also a skin rash

explanation: Assess for possible serious bacterial infection despite the apparent URTI. A seemingly minor respiratory focus does not exclude serious bacterial infection or sepsis in a young infant who looks unwell, so further assessment is still required.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because an apparent URTI should not be assumed to explain an unwell young infant without considering sepsis.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because a young infant who looks unwell requires assessment for possible serious bacterial infection even when an URTI seems present.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because supportive treatment alone would miss the need to assess for serious bacterial infection.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because sepsis assessment should not wait for fever to develop before acting.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the need for investigation depends on the infant’s age and clinical appearance, not on the presence of a rash.
